hint: I'm going to pick up Tomáš.
explain: pro + accusative. Tomáš is masculine animate (a person) and ends in soft -š, so it takes -e: Tomáše.
vidět + accusative. student is masculine animate with a hard stem (-t), so it adds -a: studenta.
potřebovat + accusative. učitel is a person (animate); nouns in -tel are soft, so they take -e: učitele.
pes is masculine animate (an animal), hard stem → -a. The -e- in 'pes' disappears: pes → psa.
otec is masculine animate. It ends in -c (soft) → -e, and the -e- of '-ec' disappears: otec → otce.
čekat na + accusative. kolega is masculine but ends in -a, so the noun changes -a → -u like žena: kolegu.
král is masculine animate. It belongs to the soft type (like muž), so it takes -e: krále. Learn it as a pair: král – krále.
pozdravovat + accusative. Jiří declines like the adjective moderní, so the masculine animate accusative is -ího: Jiřího.
pokoj is masculine INANIMATE (a thing), so the accusative is the same as the nominative: pokoj.
sešit is masculine inanimate → no change: sešit.
místnost is feminine and ends in a consonant (-ost), so it does not change: místnost.
káva is feminine in -a → -u: kávu.
kniha is feminine in -a → -u: knihu.
židle is feminine, soft type in -e → -i: židli.
město is neuter → accusative = nominative: město.
moře is neuter → no change: moře.
dovolená is a noun that declines like an adjective (česká → českou), so: dovolenou.
Petr is masculine animate with a hard stem (-r, not -ř) → -a: Petra.
ulice is feminine soft type in -e → -i: ulici.
Marek: masculine animate, hard stem → -a, and the -e- of '-ek' disappears: Marka.
lékař is masculine animate; -ř is a soft consonant → -e: lékaře.
auto is neuter → no change: auto.
Marie is feminine in -ie → -ii: Marii (like židle → židli).

hint: I have a grandfather in Brno.
explain: dědeček: animate, hard stem → -a; the last -e- disappears: dědečka.
tenista is masculine in -a → the noun takes -u: tenistu. (The pronoun stays masculine: toho.)
fotbalista: masculine in -a → -u: fotbalistu.
muž is masculine animate with soft -ž → -e: muže.
Pavel: hard type → -a, and the -e- disappears: Pavla.
kůň (horse) is animate, soft -ň → -e. The long ů becomes o: kůň → koně.
bratranec (cousin): -ec loses its -e- and -c is soft → -e: bratrance.
turista is masculine in -a → -u: turistu.
malíř (painter): animate, soft -ř → -e: malíře.
Feminine in -a → -u: ženu.
skříň (wardrobe) is feminine ending in a consonant → no change.
náměstí (square) is neuter → no change.
práce is feminine soft type in -e → -i: práci.
Němec (a German): -ec loses -e-, soft -c → -e: Němce.
telefon is masculine inanimate → no change.
kamarád (friend): animate, hard -d → -a: kamaráda.
Tomáš: animate, soft -š → -e: Tomáše.
telefon is masculine inanimate → the adjective stays like the nominative: nový.
student is masculine animate → hard adjective takes -ého: českého.
kniha is feminine → hard adjective takes -ou: zajímavou.
auto is neuter; soft adjectives keep -í: moderní.
muž is masculine animate → soft adjective takes -ího: cizího.
kamarád is masculine animate → -ího: inteligentního.
starší is a soft adjective; bratr is masculine animate → -ího: staršího.
sestra is feminine; a soft adjective keeps -í: mladší.
kabát is masculine inanimate → no change: elegantní.

hint: I'm looking for a spring jacket.
explain: bunda is feminine; soft adjective keeps -í: jarní.
dovolená is feminine; soft adjective keeps -í: aktivní.
dům is masculine inanimate → no change: velký.
pes is masculine animate (an animal) → -ého: malého.
město is neuter → hard adjective -é: hezké.
káva is feminine → -ou: dobrou.

hint: I'm looking for a new teacher.
explain: učitel is masculine animate → -ého: nového.
práce is feminine; soft adjective keeps -í: pasivní.
muž is masculine animate → ten becomes toho.
sešit is masculine inanimate → no change: ten.
Feminine: ta → tu.
Neuter: to stays to.
Masculine animate: tento → tohoto (toho + to).
Feminine: tahle → tuhle (tu + hle).
dort is masculine inanimate → no change: tenhle.
kluk is masculine animate → tenhle becomes tohohle.
bratr is masculine animate → můj becomes mého. (In the 1st person, svého is also correct.)

Neuter: tvůj → tvé or tvoje.
Masculine animate: náš → našeho.
Feminine: váš → vaši (short a, ending -i).
jeho (his) never changes: jeho psa.
její declines like moderní: masculine animate → jejího.
jejich (their) never changes.
Neuter: náš → naše.
její is like moderní: feminine stays její.

hint: Petr is looking for his OWN key.
explain: The key belongs to Petr, the subject → svůj. klíč is inanimate → svůj stays svůj. ('jeho klíč' would mean another man's key.)
The husband belongs to Jana, the subject → svůj. muž is animate → svého.

hint: Tomáš is looking for his (own) bag.
explain: The bag belongs to Tomáš (the subject) → svůj. Feminine → svou / svoji.
The car belongs to Eva (the subject) → svůj. Neuter → své / svoje.

hint: Petr is washing his brother's car (NOT his own).
explain: The car belongs to someone else (the brother), not to the subject Petr → jeho (never changes).
pes is masculine animate → tvůj becomes tvého.
Masculine animate: ten → toho, dobrý → dobrého, student → studenta. All three words agree.
Feminine: ta → tu, nová → novou, kniha → knihu.
Neuter: everything stays as in the nominative.
Masculine inanimate: no change in any of the words.

hint: I'm waiting for my older brother.
explain: Masculine animate: můj → mého, starší → staršího (soft adjective -ího), bratr → bratra.
Feminine: naše → naši, moderní stays (soft), kuchyně → kuchyni (-e → -i).
kolega is masculine animate: tvůj → tvého, nový → nového. But the noun ends in -a, so it takes -u: kolegu.
Masculine animate: toho, cizího (soft -ího), muže (soft -e).

hint: Petr is looking for my younger sister.
explain: Feminine: moje → moji / mou, mladší stays (soft), sestra → sestru.
Feminine: ta → tu; moderní stays; místnost (consonant ending) stays.
Animal = animate: toho, malého, psa (pes loses its -e-).
Masculine animate: náš → našeho, starý → starého, učitel → učitele (-tel is soft).
Neuter: nothing changes.

explain: pro ALWAYS takes the accusative: dárek pro mámu.

prompt: Which case does this preposition take?
explain: přes ALWAYS takes the accusative: přes most.

explain: skrz takes the accusative: skrz okno.

Being in a place (kde?) → na + locative: na poště.

explain: Location (kde?) → pod + instrumental: pod stolem.

hint: The cat crawled under the table (movement).

prompt: Which case does this preposition take?
explain: bez takes the GENITIVE (2nd case), not the accusative: kávu bez cukru. Don't mix it up with pro (accusative).
děkovat za (thank for) → accusative: za dárek.
v + day of the week → accusative: v pondělí, ve středu, v sobotu.
'Thank for something' = děkovat ZA + accusative. pro means 'for (someone's benefit)'.
'For someone' (who receives it) = pro + accusative.
across = přes + accusative.

čekat NA + accusative (wait for).
Days of the week: v + accusative (v pondělí, v sobotu; ve středu, ve čtvrtek).
through = skrz + accusative.
Events (koncert, film, výlet, oběd) use na. Movement → accusative: na koncert.

přes + accusative; most is masculine inanimate → no change.

zajímat se o + accusative; hudba → hudbu.
děkovat za + accusative; pomoc is feminine ending in a consonant → no change.
